claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this, I'll need to ask you some questions about your situation.

Let me start with the basics:

**How many children are you responsible for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking into claiming Child Benefit for my daughter. Her name is Alex and she's 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have a daughter named Alex who is 17 years old.

Since Alex is 17, the eligibility rules are a bit different. Let me ask:

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** For example, is she at school, college, or doing an apprenticeship?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, she's still in college doing her A-levels.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for clarifying that. So Alex is in approved education at college doing A-levels, which is positive for eligibility.

Now I need to ask about your living situation:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. And one more important question:

**Do you live with Alex, or does she live with someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: She lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Now I have one final question to confirm your eligibility:

**Are you, or your partner (if you have one), earning an individual income over £60,000 per year?** This is important because there's a tax charge that may apply to Child Benefit if income exceeds this threshold, though you would still be eligible to receive it.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, neither of us earns over £60,000.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all that information. I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Excellent news! You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's a summary of why you qualify:

✓ **Age:** Alex is 17, which falls within the eligible range
✓ **Education:** She is in approved education (A-levels at college), which allows eligibility to continue until she turns 20
✓ **Living situation:** Alex lives with you in the UK, and you are responsible for her
✓ **Income:** Neither you nor your partner earns over £60,000, so you won't be affected by the high income tax charge

You can now proceed to make a claim for Child Benefit. If you have any other children you'd like me to check eligibility for, please let me know!
